en: The *Tulajāṣṭaka*, composed by the illustrious and primordial Śaṅkarācārya.
Her limbs are as beautiful and radiant as the moon, jasmine, and milk; her body is adorned with necklaces of pearls;
she is clad in white garments, and her form is languid from the weight of her breasts.
I bow to the primordial Tulajābhavānī. ||1||
She whose garments are red, whose eyes are large and red, and who wears necklaces of rubies and pearls upon her neck that surpass the radiance of the rising sun.
I bow to the primordial Tulajābhavānī. ||2||
Her body is dark-complexioned, her eyes are like those of a young fawn,
she is clothed in silken garments, and she is worshipped with flowers;
her limbs are anointed with musk and sandalwood.
I bow to Tulajābhavānī, the primordial Śāmā.
Clad in yellow garments, with the luster of a campaka flower, fair-complexioned, and adorned with the finest ornaments—
[I bow] to her who was born on earth for the destruction of the demons.
I bow to Tulajābhavānī, the primordial one. ||4||
Wearing the sun and moon as earrings, three-eyed, bearing a trident, and possessing an exceedingly terrible form,
she holds her weapons for the destruction of adversaries.
I bow to Tulajābhavānī, the primordial Śamā.
She who is worshipped by Brahmā, Indra, Nārāyaṇa, and Rudra;
she who is celebrated in song by celestial nymphs;
and she who is praised with words by sages such as Nārada.
I bow to Tulajābhavānī, who is primordial and beyond the reach of the mind.
She who is meditated upon by Sanaka and others through the eightfold yoga, who is attainable through samādhi by the lords of sages,
and who is the eternal wish-fulfilling cow for the devotee;
I bow to Tulajābhavānī, the primordial Śāmā.
Seated upon a lion-throne, being fanned by all the gods with beautiful whisks,
she held a parasol of exceedingly bright color.
I bow to Tulajābhavānī, the primordial Śamā.
May the full side-glance of the Mother of all the worlds,
who bestows life upon those who worship the Daughter of the Mountain King,
never bring poverty to people at any time.
Whence could there be anxiety for one who has crossed the ocean of existence? ||9||
The man who recites this hymn, the Tulajāṣṭaka, at the three periods of the day shall obtain long life, fame, glory, and prosperity.
One shall obtain wealth and sons. ||10||
Thus ends the hymn to the goddess Atulajādevī composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
